title: Cross-tenant headroom accounting mismatch causing transient burst overcommit
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: During a customer-reported outage on 2026-03-10 we observed several Dedicated reserved pools transiently enter an overcommitted state and subsequently throttle customer traffic for multiple tenants. This incident was reproducible when multiple high-burst tenants attempted concurrent burst allocations. Initial mitigation was applied within 2 hours and a hotfix patch was deployed to stop immediate customer impact.

Root cause hypothesis and evidence: A change merged in runtime-1.22 to optimize KV/prefix cache memory accounting introduced an arithmetic mismatch between the autoscaler headroom calculator and the burst admission controller. The autoscaler computes 'available GPU headroom' based on reserved slots minus active allocations plus an estimate of cached KV memory that can be reclaimed. The new cache estimate was being double-applied in two places: (1) the headroom estimator and (2) the burst admission buffer. Under concurrent burst requests from different tenants, this double-crediting made headroom appear larger than it actually was, allowing the admission controller to grant bursts beyond physical capacity. When the autoscaler observed the sudden increase in queueing, it started a delayed scale-up but also applied an aggressive scale-down policy configured earlier, which caused late scale-down events to remove capacity that was actually in use by active allocations with non-evictable KV footprints. This combination produced transient overcommit and dropped request tails.

Reproduction steps: 1) Start three simulated tenants with burst profiles matching customer telemetry (token-rate spikes to 8x baseline for ~30s every 2 minutes). 2) Enable prefix-cache-optimizations flag and the aggressive scale-down config. 3) Fire bursts concurrently and observe reserved pool headroom metric exceed physical capacity and admission success followed by kernel OOM/slot preemption logs. 4) Verified logs: runtime/allocator: headroom_estimate=18, physical_slots_available=12, admission_granted=6 -> actual backpressure and OOM traces following.

Immediate mitigations (applied 2026-03-10): - Emergency config: set autoscaler.scale_down_min_delay to 10m to prevent late scale-downs during burst windows. - Admission throttling: globally reduce burst_admission_margin from 20% to 2% for affected pools. - Rollout: patched and rolled runtime hotfix to stop using the new cache estimate in the admission path (PR and rollback links below). These steps restored stability for impacted tenants within ~90 minutes.

Planned permanent fixes: - Correct accounting: remove duplicate cache-crediting and centralize headroom calculation into a single well-tested surface. - Add ownership semantics for non-evictable KV entries so autoscaler treats them as locked capacity. - BDD/e2e workload simulations to exercise concurrent multi-tenant bursts and autoscaler policies. - Add an alert when admission_granted > physical_slots_available * 0.95 for 30s. - Backfill unit and integration tests to cover the arithmetic edge cases and concurrency windows.

Rollout plan: 1) Land accounting fix behind feature flag and run canary against internal stressbench for 48h. 2) If green, progressively roll to 10% of Dedicated pools, monitor headroom vs actual metrics for 24h. 3) Full rollout and disable emergency throttles. 4) Post-rollout audit and customer-facing incident summary.

Follow-ups and ownership: Andre Soto (assignee) owns the code fix and canary. SRE (oncall rotation) to own emergency config changes and dashboards. PM and Customer Success to coordinate communications for impacted customers and verify SLA credits if required.
